request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've implemented dated holds, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed in behaviour**
- **Holds:** a person can now have several holds over time. Each has a from-date (blank means the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, both inclusive. A hold with no to-date runs open-ended, and a hold ends on its to-date, so there is no release action any more.
- **Totals:** only open claims (OPEN or PENDING) dated within a hold are left out of the live totals. A claim bound by a statement stays in whatever its date, and settled claims always count. The same rule applies everywhere totals are worked out: per-person and sheet totals, the ROLLUP/TOTALS audit lines, statements, closing a period, and the screen's due-totals, period totals and overdue figures.
- **Screen:** "Held" shows yes if the person has any hold at all, even one in the past or future. The row lists each hold as a `person-hold-line` and has from/to inputs with the Hold button. Bad dates, or a to-date before the from-date, show `person-error` and write nothing.
- **Audit:** holding writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=<name> from=<date>`. The to-date isn't recorded, as the request specified. `PERSON_RELEASED` is gone.

**Stored data**
- A new migration, `V30__person_hold.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table and drops the old `held` flag.
- Anyone on hold before this change gets a hold with no from- or to-date, so it covers all dates as the old flag did.

**Decision for you:** taking a statement keeps an already-bound claim inside a hold bound, because it still counts. Unbound open claims inside a hold aren't bound. The other option is for a new statement to re-check holds and unbind those claims. Say if you'd prefer that.

The main changes are in `person/HoldPerson.java`, `ValidateHold.java`, `Hold.java`, `PersonRepository.java` and `Claim.counts`, and on the front end in `features/hold/hold.slot.tsx` and `features/claims/useClaims.ts`.
